editorial.headline: Agricultural Speciality Retail: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Nationally open to full foreign ownership, this specialist agricultural retail activity is nevertheless blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the province’s permanent risk-based moratorium.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor, the decisive fact about this specialist agricultural retail activity is not its national openness but its present position in Bali: it cannot be registered there for PMA today. Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA—open to foreign investment—with foreign ownership permitted up to 100 per cent. Bali, however, blocks it for PMA registration under the province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium for Low- and Medium-Low-risk KBLI activities. This is a geographic restriction that sits alongside the national position.

The scope is specialist retail trade in agricultural produce. Its recognisable commodities include pepper, nutmeg, turmeric, kencur, temulawak, galangal and honey—items that place spices, rhizomes and honey at the centre of the retail offer. This is therefore a defined agricultural-products retail activity, rather than a description of a single commodity. The examples show the breadth of merchandise within the stated specialist focus, while keeping the activity anchored in agricultural produce.

The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar businesses. That range tells founders that the same stated activity is available across the four listed business scales; it does not change the nature of the specialist retail scope. A business may frame its registration around the retail sale of these agricultural commodities while remaining within one of the record’s permitted scales. At the national level, the PMA position is equally unambiguous: the maximum foreign ownership figure is 100 per cent.

Bali changes the practical conclusion for PMA. At the Besar scale, OSS assigns every scope a Low or Medium-Low risk position, and the record identifies that risk treatment as the reason the Bali moratorium applies. The moratorium was recorded in May 2026 and blocks PMA across the island for all activities in those two risk bands; it is described as permanent. Nationally open does not mean available for PMA registration in Bali. The accurate conclusion is simply that this activity remains open nationally, while a foreigner cannot register it in Bali today under the stated moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open does not mean available for PMA registration in Bali.
